title: Free Accessibility Tools Directory
subtitle: Free screen readers, magnifiers, dictation, captions, reading aids, and ADHD / low-energy helpers
credits: Published by Asdale Dynamics, LLC (Indiana, formed Oct 2026). Beginner-friendly AI education, books, and practical tools.

tools.name: NVDA
tools.costDetail: Free and open source; donations welcome
tools.setup: Download the installer from nvaccess.org, run it, and follow the first-time setup (choose keyboard layout and speak-up preferences). Press Insert+N to open the NVDA menu anytime.

tools.name: VoiceOver (macOS)
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver and turn it on. Press Command+F5 to toggle. The first launch offers a VoiceOver tutorial to learn the cursor and commands.

tools.name: VoiceOver (iOS)
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver and turn it on. Use the Accessibility Shortcut (triple-click the side or Home button) to toggle it quickly.

tools.name: Narrator
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows at no extra cost
tools.setup: Press Windows+Ctrl+Enter to turn Narrator on or off. Open Settings > Accessibility > Narrator to change voices, speed, and verbosity.

tools.name: TalkBack
tools.costDetail: Built into Android at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > TalkBack and turn it on. Hold both volume keys for 3 seconds to toggle TalkBack (enable the shortcut first).

tools.name: Orca
tools.costDetail: Free and open source
tools.setup: Preinstalled on many GNOME-based distributions. Enable it in Settings > Accessibility > Screen Reader, or install the 'orca' package with your distro's package manager.

tools.name: ChromeVox
tools.costDetail: Free and open source
tools.setup: On Chromebooks, press Ctrl+Alt+Z to toggle ChromeVox. On other computers, add the ChromeVox extension from the Chrome Web Store.

tools.name: Windows Magnifier
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows at no extra cost
tools.setup: Press Windows+Plus (+) to zoom in and Windows+Minus (-) to zoom out. Press Windows+Esc to close. Choose full-screen, docked, or lens view in Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.

tools.name: macOS Zoom
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Zoom and enable 'Use keyboard shortcuts to zoom' or 'Use scroll gesture with modifier keys to zoom'. Toggle with Option+Command+8.

tools.name: iOS Zoom
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Zoom and turn it on. Double-tap with three fingers to zoom, drag three fingers to move around the screen.

tools.name: Android Magnification
tools.costDetail: Built into Android at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Magnification and choose a shortcut (triple-tap screen or accessibility button). Tap the shortcut to magnify the part of the screen you touch.

tools.name: KMag
tools.costDetail: Free and open source
tools.setup: Install the 'kmag' package using your distribution's package manager (part of KDE Gear), then launch KMag from your applications menu.

tools.name: Windows Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows 11 at no extra cost
tools.setup: Press Windows+Ctrl+L to turn Live Captions on. Download the language pack when prompted, then choose your caption style and microphone source in Settings > Accessibility > Captions.

tools.name: macOS Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions (beta) and turn it on. Captions appear in a floating window for any audio playing on your Mac.

tools.name: Chrome Live Caption
tools.costDetail: Built into the Chrome browser at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Chrome Settings > Accessibility and turn on Live Caption. Captions appear automatically for videos and audio playing in Chrome tabs.

tools.name: Live Transcribe & Sound Notifications
tools.costDetail: Free app from Google
tools.setup: Install Live Transcribe from the Play Store, then enable it in Settings > Accessibility > Live Transcribe. It transcribes speech in real time and can alert you to sounds like doorbells or alarms.

tools.name: iOS Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS 16 and later at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions (beta) and turn it on. Type-to-speak responses are also supported during FaceTime and phone calls.

tools.name: Windows Voice Access
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows 11 at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Speech > Voice Access and turn it on. Download the language pack when prompted, then say 'Voice Access wake up' to begin controlling your PC by voice.

tools.name: Windows Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows at no extra cost
tools.setup: Press Windows+H in any text field to start dictation. Say punctuation like 'period' or 'comma' as you speak. Enable online speech recognition in Settings > Privacy & security > Speech.

tools.name: macOS Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and turn it on. Press the Fn key (or the Dictation key) twice to start speaking wherever you can type.

tools.name: iOS Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > General > Keyboard and turn on Enable Dictation. Tap the microphone icon on the keyboard to dictate text in any app.

tools.name: macOS Voice Control
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control and turn it on. Number overlays and a grid let you click, scroll, and navigate entirely by voice.

tools.name: iOS Voice Control
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control and turn it on. Use numbered item overlays or a screen grid to tap, swipe, and type by voice.

tools.name: Gboard Voice Typing
tools.costDetail: Free keyboard app from Google
tools.setup: Install Gboard from the Play Store (Android) or App Store (iOS), set it as your keyboard, then tap the microphone icon on the keyboard to dictate text.

tools.name: Microsoft Immersive Reader
tools.costDetail: Built into Edge, OneNote, Word, and Outlook at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open a web page in Microsoft Edge and press F9 (or select the Immersive Reader icon in the address bar). Use it to read aloud, change text size, spacing, fonts, and highlight parts of speech.

tools.name: macOS Spoken Content
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content. Enable 'Speak selection' and choose a keyboard shortcut, or turn on 'Speak screen' to have items read aloud.

tools.name: iOS Spoken Content
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content. Turn on Speak Selection and Speak Screen, then swipe down with two fingers from the top of the screen to hear page content read aloud.

tools.name: Android Select to Speak
tools.costDetail: Built into Android at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Select to Speak and turn it on. Tap the Play button or tap items on screen to hear them read aloud.

tools.name: OpenDyslexic
tools.costDetail: Free and open source font
tools.setup: Download the font from opendyslexic.org and install it on your system, or add a browser extension that renders pages in OpenDyslexic.

tools.name: OpenAI Whisper (local)
tools.costDetail: Free and open source; runs locally on your own computer
tools.setup: Install Whisper (pip install openai-whisper) or use a desktop front end such as Whisper.cpp. Drop in an audio file and get a local transcript with no data leaving your computer.

tools.name: Goblin.tools
tools.costDetail: Free web tools (donations welcome)
tools.setup: Open goblin.tools in any browser. Use Magic To-Do to break big jobs into steps, Formalizer to rewrite text, Estimator for time, and Compiler to turn brain dumps into task lists. No account required.

tools.name: Habitica
tools.costDetail: Free tier; optional paid subscription
tools.setup: Create a free account at habitica.com, add habits, dailies, and to-dos, and check them off to earn in-game rewards. Works well for low-energy days because small wins still count.

tools.name: Pomofocus
tools.costDetail: Free web timer (optional account)
tools.setup: Open pomofocus.io, set your work and break intervals, and start the timer. A simple Pomodoro loop helps when starting is the hardest part.

tools.name: Microsoft To Do
tools.costDetail: Free with a Microsoft account
tools.setup: Sign in with a free Microsoft account, create a list (try 'Today'), and add tasks. Use 'My Day' to pick a few small tasks each morning so lists stay manageable.

tools.name: Trello
tools.costDetail: Free tier with unlimited cards and up to 10 boards per workspace
tools.setup: Create a free account at trello.com, make a board, add lists (To Do / Doing / Done), and drop cards on them. Drag-and-drop boards work well for visual thinkers.

tools.name: macOS Switch Control
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Switch Control and turn it on. Connect one or more adaptive switches and use scanning to navigate and control your Mac.

tools.name: iOS Switch Control
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Switch Control and turn it on. Pair adaptive switches or use the screen as a trigger to scan and select items.
